title: Emergency Notice: Zones 3 and 4
speaker: Marrow Bay City Office
text:
ZONES 3 AND 4 ARE UNDER EVACUATION ORDER.
Coaches leave Harbour Avenue every twenty minutes until 03:00. Carry nothing larger than one bag.

Do not drink from taps in Zones 3, 4 or 5 until the water office clears them.

If a member of your household is unwell, elderly, or cannot walk to the coach, do NOT wait with them. Mark the door with tape and report the address at the plaza checkpoint.

This notice is issued on the authority of Chief W. Hale, Marrow Bay Police.

title: Note under a wiper blade
speaker: Dinah
text:
Rob - if you get back to the car before me, we went on foot. The avenue is solid, nobody is moving. I have Ellie and your mother.

They would not let your mother on the coach. The officer said she'd slow the aisle. I'm not leaving her in the flat with tape on the door, I don't care what the notice says.

We are going up to the plaza. If the plaza is shut we are going to the station, there are police there at least.

Don't wait at the car. Please.

title: Unsent letter in a jacket pocket
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
Cris - I'm writing this in the ambulance bay because I can't say it on the phone.

Something happened at the port the night before last and we were told not to write it up. Not told. Ordered, in person, by the chief, to eleven of us in a room with the door shut.

I did write it up. It's in the archive where it belongs and I kept the key on me, which is probably stupid of me.

If I'm slow coming home this week that's why. Feed the cat.

title: Body camera 4471, clip A: Yard C, 17:38
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
Night rain, floodlights, the side of a container with VGR-7718 stencilled on it. Six officers in port police jackets, none of them port police.

Three federal agents are kneeling on the wet concrete with their hands flat on their heads. The tall one keeps talking.

PRUITT (off camera): "Agent Dale Pruitt. Federal. That container is evidence, Chief."
HALE: "Then it's police evidence now."
PRUITT: "You don't have the authority and you know it."
HALE: "Put him in a van."

A younger agent moves and someone fires twice. The camera jerks to the ground, then up. The tall one is walking to the van with an officer's hand on his neck. Hale is holding his own forearm and looking at it.

RUIZ (close, quiet): "Four-four-seven-one, I'm still recording."

title: Body camera 4471, clip B: station lobby, 01:12
speaker: Ana Ruiz
text:
The watch desk. Ruiz's hand comes into frame and hangs a key on the duty board, then takes it back off again.

RUIZ: "Logging it out properly. Evidence room, one key, Ruiz."
DESK OFFICER: "You're not supposed to have that."
RUIZ: "Then write that down too."

She walks into the archive. The camera swings across rolling stacks and stops on a records cabinet with brass letter plates. Her hand pulls out her own drawer, drops the key inside, and slides it shut.

RUIZ: "My drawer, my mess."

The clip ends in the corridor. Somebody is screaming two floors down.

title: Watch desk duty log, night shift
text:
KEYS OUT / KEYS IN - NIGHT SHIFT

22:40 Garage 2 - Okonjo - returned 23:55
23:15 Cell block - Dolan - NOT RETURNED
00:20 Armoury cage - Hale - NOT RETURNED
01:12 Evidence room - Ruiz - NOT RETURNED (see note)
01:30 Archive - Ruiz - returned 01:41

Note added by desk: Ruiz was told twice she is not on the evidence list this month. She logged it anyway. Taking it up with the sergeant when the sergeant exists again.

02:05 Everything after this is on the floor somewhere, we stopped writing.

title: Records cabinet index card
text:
PERSONAL RECORDS CABINET - HOW IT WORKS

One drawer per serving officer, filed by surname letter, A at the top left to Z at the bottom right. Shared letters share a drawer.

Your drawer is for your own notebooks, court diaries and personal property while on shift. It is NOT an evidence store. It is NOT a key store. We have a duty board for keys.

Drawers do not lock. That is deliberate. If you need something locked, ask the custody sergeant.

- Records clerk

title: Custody log, page torn at the corner
text:
CELL 1 - empty
CELL 2 - male, no name given, no charge entered. Brought in 18:40 with the other one. Deceased 19:05. Doctor not called.
CELL 3 - empty
CELL 4 - male, no name given, no charge entered. Brought in 18:40. Injury to left forearm, dressed by officers, medic refused.

Across the bottom in a different hand: NO RECORD. CHIEF'S ORDERS. DO NOT ENTER THESE TWO IN THE SYSTEM.

Under that, in pencil: I am entering them in this book because this book is not the system.

title: Evidence intake sheet, locker 17
speaker: Custody Sgt. Okonjo
text:
LOCKER 17 - COURT SEAL

Contents: one bound ledger, hard cover, handwritten. Seized from a vehicle on Harbour Avenue, 11 Sep. Marked V.B. PAYMENTS on the spine.

Sealed on the application of CID. Under seal this locker cannot be opened from the cell block or from here. The bolt releases from the CID desk terminal and only from there, with an authorised print.

Do not cut the bolt. Do not ask me to cut the bolt. Det. Sgt. Ferris has been very clear that this one goes to court in one piece.

title: Booking print cards, sleeve of three
text:
Three grey cards in one plastic sleeve, each with ten inked boxes and a classification line at the top.

CARD 1 - MARSH, D. - booked 02 Aug, affray - RIGHT INDEX: LOOP - ridge count 9
CARD 2 - FERRIS, M., Det. Sgt. - booked 14 Sep, complaint withdrawn same day - RIGHT INDEX: WHORL - ridge count 14
CARD 3 - UNKNOWN MALE - booked 18:40 last night, no charge entered - RIGHT INDEX: ARCH - ridge count 11

On the back of card 2, in biro: "Booked by his own chief on a Monday and back at his desk by Tuesday. Whole thing was a message."

title: Confiscated recorder, property bag 7-C
speaker: Dale Pruitt
text:
Pruitt, continuing. Whoever finds this, the tape is the report.

We landed at the port at thirteen hundred. The container was already open and already wrong. Cold mist still coming off the floor of it at eleven hours.

The port police turned up with the chief of a city force that has no business at a port. They took Ortiz's camera and they took the manifests.

I got my hand on the chief's arm and he pulled away like I'd burned him. He had a dressing under the sleeve. He has been bitten and he is walking around giving orders.

If you are federal, go up. Not out. Up.

title: Re: V.B. ledger - please read before Friday
speaker: Det. Sgt. M. Ferris
text:
To: K. Abiola, County Prosecutor's Office
From: M. Ferris, Marrow Bay CID

Kemi - the book is real and it is in my evidence room under seal, locker 17.

Six transfers over seven months from a Vigor Biotech holding account to an account in the chief's wife's maiden name. Two of the six came back the same week, I assume because somebody at their end got nervous. Four of them cleared and stayed cleared.

I want the four, not the six. The four are the case.

He had me booked and printed last month on a complaint that evaporated by lunchtime. I know what that was. Please move fast.

title: PrintLock 2 quick guide, taped to the monitor
text:
CID DESK TERMINAL - SEAL RELEASE

1. Wake the pad. The screen shows the last print this terminal accepted, as a classification and a ridge count. That is the print the seal is registered to.
2. Lay the booking card face down on the glass, square to the arrows. The pad reads the inked right index box.
3. Match on classification AND ridge count. A wrong card is not a free guess: three wrong reads lock the pad for ninety seconds and sound the desk alarm.
4. On a match the terminal releases the bolt on the named locker. Go and open it by hand. The terminal does not open anything up here.

title: CID desk terminal, standby screen
text:
MARROW BAY CID - PRINTLOCK 2

SEAL REGISTERED: EVIDENCE LOCKER 17
STATUS: BOLTED

LAST ACCEPTED PRINT
  Digit ....... RIGHT INDEX
  Pattern ..... WHORL
  Ridge count . 14
  Accepted .... 14 Sep, 16:52

PLACE CARD ON GLASS

title: Payments ledger, spine marked V.B. PAYMENTS
text:
Received, acct. G. Mabry (maiden)

11 Mar | VGR-0431 | 8,000 | RETURNED 14 Mar
02 Apr | VGR-0588 | 7,500 | CLEARED
19 May | VGR-0613 | 2,000 | CLEARED
07 Jul | VGR-0742 | 9,250 | RETURNED 09 Jul
23 Aug | VGR-0810 | 4,000 | CLEARED
14 Sep | VGR-0917 | 1,500 | CLEARED

Last page, different pen: 0917 is the last one. Tell them the port is covered and the paper is gone. After this I am done taking it.

title: Desk diary, inside the back cover
speaker: Warren Hale
text:
Gwen asked me again where the number is written. Nowhere. I am not that stupid.

It is in the book, and only if you already know what you are looking at. Not the dates. Not the references. The money, and only the money that stayed.

What cleared, nothing that came back. The lead figure off each one. Oldest first. Four of them, four digits, in they go.

If you cannot work that out you have no business in my safe, and if you can work it out you were already in the book, which means I have bigger problems than the safe.

title: Desk diary, last written page
speaker: Warren Hale
text:
Third day.

The arm stopped hurting on the second day, which the leaflet in the Vigor crate says is normal and is not good news.

I took four of their injectors out of the shipment before it went up the coast. One in the morning, one at night, and the shaking stops for about nine hours. I am out at the end of this one.

I ran a city tonight on nine hours at a time. I signed the evacuation order. I kept my hands in my pockets on the radio call so nobody saw.

I am not going to a hospital. I know what is in me, I signed for it.

title: Shipment clearance - final confirmation
speaker: Vigor Biotech, Logistics
text:
To: Chief W. Hale
Cc: Dr. E. Voss, Research Director

Chief - confirming your clearance is on file for the Halvern movement, container VGR-7718, declared as medical supplies. Port police attendance appreciated.

Dr. Voss asks me to pass on that the municipal water contract renewal goes to committee next month and that your letter of support would be welcome. He notes the city will see the benefit of the programme before the committee does.

As ever, nothing in this chain is for your records.

title: Framed photograph on the office wall
text:
A ribbon cutting in bright daylight. Marrow Bay Water Treatment Works, reservoir 2 behind a row of clipped shrubs.

Chief Hale in dress uniform holds one end of the ribbon. A thin man in a pale suit holds the shears and is not looking at the camera; he is looking up at the intake tower.

The brass plate under the glass reads: MUNICIPAL SUPPLY MODERNISATION, OPERATED UNDER CONTRACT BY VIGOR BIOTECH. And under that, a line of smaller letters: EVERY HOUSE ON ONE LINE.

title: Notice wired to the checkpoint board
speaker: Vigor Biotech Water Services
text:
PLANNED WORKS - MARROW BAY SUPPLY

A full-system line flush is scheduled from 06:00 tomorrow and will run from the treatment works through all five zones. Pressure may vary. Discolouration is normal.

During a flush the whole network is fed from one dosing point at the works. This is routine.

No household action is required. Taps will be safe to use from the moment the flush begins.

Queries: Vigor Biotech Water Services, 24h line. Please do not call the police with water enquiries.

title: Dispatch recorder, channel 1, 02:4x
speaker: Dispatcher Yara Senn
text:
All units, I have no units. I'm reading back what I've got.

Twelve calls on the same block, all of them saying the same sentence about somebody who was ill getting up.

Chief's instruction at zero one forty is that nothing goes out on channel 1 that uses the word outbreak. I have written that down twice now so it is somebody else's problem as well as mine.

If anyone is hearing this later: we were never short of officers tonight. We were short of orders.

title: Scratched into the paint of cell 2
speaker: Sam Whitlock
text:
WHITLOCK S. FEDERAL. HELD WITHOUT CHARGE BY MARROW BAY PD ON ORDERS OF CHIEF HALE.

ORTIZ DOWN AT THE PORT.

PRUITT IN THE NEXT ONE BUT ONE. HE IS BITTEN. THEY KNOW AND THEY SHUT THE HATCH ANYWAY.

IF YOU ARE READING THIS AND YOU ARE ONE OF OURS, DO NOT GO ALONE TO THE TOWER. HE WILL TELL YOU TO. GO ANYWAY.

title: Maintenance board, sub-level
speaker: Building Services
text:
SUB-LEVEL - OPEN FAULTS

1. Sump pump 2 has failed. Standing water in the long store will be ankle deep by morning and worse if it rains. Chased three times.
2. The floor conduit down there is the old kind, in the slab, and it leaks. If the floor is wet, the floor is live when the ring is energised.
3. PANEL A and PANEL B on the walkway feed that ring. Both must be thrown together or the interlock trips.
4. Nobody stands on that floor with the ring energised. Not for a second. I have put this in writing so that when it happens it is in writing.

title: Works map in a cracked frame
speaker: Marrow Bay Drainage Board
text:
STORM INTERCEPTOR - CENTRAL SECTION

The interceptor runs north from the station sump under Harbour Avenue, crosses the plaza, and ends in the service level of the Vigor Biotech building on Crown Street, where it ties into their intake.

Access hatches are police, drainage board and Vigor Biotech only.

Handwritten in the corner: tie-in rebuilt last spring at their expense, their pumps, their doors, their keys. We maintain the pipe and nothing else. Ask them.

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: MARA
text: That's a city. I grew up looking at that skyline and it was never this quiet.

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: LEON
text: Half of them got out. The coaches are gone from the ramps.

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: MARA
text: And the other half?

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: LEON
text: Stay behind me in the water.

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: MARA
text: Where are we going?

title: Coming ashore at Marrow Bay
speaker: LEON
text: Police station. Hale signed for that container. Somewhere in that building is the paper that proves it.

title: Harbour Avenue
speaker: MARA
text: They left the bus doors open. Like they thought people were still coming.

title: Harbour Avenue
speaker: LEON
text: See the big one by the kiosk? We go around. Not through.

title: Harbour Avenue
speaker: MARA
text: It's wearing a stab vest.

title: Harbour Avenue
speaker: LEON
text: Then it was fit and strong this morning. Around.

title: Officer Ruiz in the underpass
speaker: MARA
text: Leon. There's a police officer in the water.

title: Officer Ruiz in the underpass
speaker: LEON
text: Ruiz. She's been shot, not bitten.

title: Officer Ruiz in the underpass
speaker: MARA
text: Shot by what?

title: Officer Ruiz in the underpass
speaker: LEON
text: Her camera's still on the mount, and it's still got charge. We'll let it tell us.

title: The plaza checkpoint
speaker: LEON
text: Sandbags, floodlight, nobody manning it. They built this and then left it.

title: The plaza checkpoint
speaker: MARA
text: Two of the big ones on the fountain. We can't go around this one.

title: The plaza checkpoint
speaker: LEON
text: Then we give them somewhere else to be. Scrap and a bottle. Throw it long, stay low, move when they turn.

title: The plaza checkpoint
speaker: MARA
text: You've done this before.

title: The plaza checkpoint
speaker: LEON
text: Not with company. Keep up.

title: The station lobby
speaker: MARA
text: The watch desk radio is live. Four channels and a repeater on the roof.

title: The station lobby
speaker: LEON
text: Then this is where you are. Door's steel, one way in, and I'll be inside the building.

title: The station lobby
speaker: MARA
text: I came all this way to not come with you.

title: The station lobby
speaker: LEON
text: You came all this way to be the person who can see the whole floor plan. There's a board behind you with every room on it.

title: The station lobby
speaker: MARA
text: Fine. Clip the spare set on. If you stop answering I'm coming through that building with a chair leg.

title: The station lobby
speaker: LEON
text: Noted.

title: After the body camera
speaker: MARA
text: They had him on his knees. His own people were already down and he was still arguing the law at them.

title: After the body camera
speaker: LEON
text: That's Pruitt. He'd argue the law at a fire.

title: After the body camera
speaker: MARA
text: They put him in a van, Leon. Vans come here.

title: After the body camera
speaker: LEON
text: Then he's downstairs in a cell with no paperwork. Second clip. Ruiz put the evidence key somewhere she shouldn't have.

title: After the body camera
speaker: MARA
text: Her own drawer, in the archive. She says it on camera. Brass letters on the cabinet.

title: Hint: the evidence room key
speaker: MARA
text: Nobody hid that key, Leon. Somebody filed it. Think like the woman who filed it.

title: Hint: the evidence room key
speaker: MARA
text: The duty log has her name on the evidence key at one twelve, and the cabinet card says one drawer per officer, by surname.

title: Hint: the evidence room key
speaker: MARA
text: Ruiz. R. Pull the R drawer and stop being thorough about it.

title: Hint: the print lock
speaker: MARA
text: A sealed locker that only opens from a desk upstairs. Somebody wanted exactly one person able to open it.

title: Hint: the print lock
speaker: MARA
text: The pad is telling you what it will accept. Right index, whorl, fourteen ridges. You're carrying three cards, read the tops of them.

title: Hint: the print lock
speaker: MARA
text: The detective's own card. Ferris. Hale had him printed to scare him and left the one print that opens his own locker sitting in evidence.

title: Hint: the safe code
speaker: MARA
text: He wrote a whole page about not writing it down. That page is the instructions.

title: Hint: the safe code
speaker: MARA
text: Not the dates, not the reference numbers. The money that stayed. Four of the six cleared, and he wants the first figure off each, oldest first.

title: Hint: the safe code
speaker: MARA
text: Seven thousand five, two thousand, four thousand, one thousand five. Seven, two, four, one. Try it.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Took you long enough.

title: Cell 4
speaker: LEON
text: Dale. Let me get the hatch.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Leave the hatch. Look at my arm and then leave the hatch.

title: Cell 4
speaker: LEON
text: I have a suppressant.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Nine hours at a time. That's what it buys. I've been in here nine of those.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Listen while I'm still me. Voss isn't at the port and he isn't on your island. He's in the tower on Crown Street. Floor thirty-five, the lab with his name on the door.

title: Cell 4
speaker: LEON
text: Thirty-five. How do you know that?

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Hale came down here to look at me. He talks when he's frightened. He kept saying it won't matter by six.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Vigor runs the city's water. At six they flush the whole network off one dosing point and Voss puts his work in the line. Every tap, Leon. All five zones before the buses come back.

title: Cell 4
speaker: LEON
text: Two hours.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Two hours. Ortiz went at the port, Whitlock went in the next cell, and I'm not going to be the thing that gets out of this one.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: You know what I'm asking. Don't make me say it twice, I'm tired.

title: Cell 4
speaker: LEON
text: I heard you the first time.

title: Cell 4
speaker: PRUITT
text: Good. Then go up, not out. And Leon - the chief is still in this building.

title: After the cells
speaker: MARA
text: Leon. I heard a door and then I heard nothing for four minutes.

title: After the cells
speaker: LEON
text: Found my team leader.

title: After the cells
speaker: MARA
text: Is he -

title: After the cells
speaker: LEON
text: He told me where Voss is and what happens at six. That's what he did with the last of it. Write it down: Crown Street tower, floor thirty-five, the water flush at six.

title: After the cells
speaker: MARA
text: Written down. Leon - I'm not going to ask you anything else about the cells.

title: After the cells
speaker: LEON
text: Thanks.

title: The stairs down
speaker: MARA
text: The board down here says sub-level long store. There's a fault card pinned over it in red.

title: The stairs down
speaker: LEON
text: Flooded, and the conduit's in the slab. I read the same note.

title: The stairs down
speaker: MARA
text: Two panels, thrown together. Which means you need to be somewhere dry when you do it.

title: The stairs down
speaker: LEON
text: There's a walkway. Stay off the channel for a while.

title: The sewer door
speaker: MARA
text: Leon, talk to me. The whole building just went dark and came back.

title: The sewer door
speaker: LEON
text: Hale's done. He told me the truth first, for whatever that's worth at four in the morning.

title: The sewer door
speaker: MARA
text: And the door?

title: The sewer door
speaker: LEON
text: Open. The map says this pipe comes up inside their building. Bring the lamp and come down the back stair. We're not waiting for six o'clock.
